title: MTIA 300: Meta’s First Training Chip Featuring Built-in NICs and Collective Offloading Engines
evidence_span: Meta’s official Engineering post describes MTIA 300 as a training accelerator optimized for ranking and recommendation models, with network chiplets containing twelve custom 800 Gbps RDMA NICs, 1.2 TB/s total I/O bandwidth, and flexible partitioning between scale-up and scale-out traffic. Sixteen dedicated message engines offload collectives, with near-memory reduction throughput above 2.8 TB/s. HCCL is co-designed with the chip and compiles collectives into autonomous work graphs. Meta reports less than 0.5% compute-throughput degradation during concurrent large GEMMs and collectives, up to 940 GB/s rack communication, and 3.9x faster total communication than an equivalent GPU cluster on a 150B-parameter production recommendation model across 40 accelerators.
problem: Recommendation-model training is communication-bound because embedding tables contain most model parameters and hybrid parallelism generates frequent AllReduce, AllToAll, and AllGather operations that compete with computation on GPU resources.
method_or_artifact: MTIA 300 co-designs compute, integrated network chiplets, dedicated message engines, near-memory collective reduction, and the HCCL communication library; collectives are compiled into autonomous dependency graphs rather than launched as compute-grid kernels.
workload_or_benchmark: Production ranking and recommendation-model training, including a 150-billion-parameter model across 40 accelerators; rack-scale and cross-rack collective communication are evaluated.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: MTIA 300 with twelve 800 Gbps RDMA NICs, sixteen message engines, HBM, scale-up/scale-out Ethernet domains, and Meta’s HCCL/PyTorch software stack; exact silicon process, power, area, and workload-selection methodology require paper verification.
baselines: general-purpose GPU cluster with GPU-resident collective communication
metrics: more than 2.8 TB/s collective reduction throughput
less than 0.5% compute-throughput degradation during concurrent GEMM and collectives
up to 940 GB/s rack communication bandwidth
3.9x faster total communication than equivalent GPU cluster
limits: The evidence is an official Meta Engineering article, not the captured IEEE paper or an independent audit. Production comparisons, power/area/cost, model mix, cluster configuration, and whether communication or end-to-end training is the reported bottleneck require full-paper verification.
